title: A dense henselian valued subfield is relatively separably closed
statement: Let $K\hookrightarrow L$ be a field extension [def-pc-field-extension] with nontrivial valuations [def-trf-valuation-ring]. Assume the valuation ring of $K$ is henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], that the valuation topology of $K$ is induced from $L$, and that the image of $K$ is dense in $L$ (every nonempty open subset meets it). Then every $a\in L$ separable over $K$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension] belongs to the image of $K$. No henselianity of $L$, completeness, rank, or residue-characteristic condition is imposed.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed p.374: dense embedding of henselian valued fields and the displayed Galois-group isomorphism.

proof.text: For a separable a over K, put E=K(a). Embed E in a separable closure and then in a finite Galois extension N/K. Prolong the henselian valuation of K to N. The topology on E inherited from N and the topology inherited from L both induce the given topology on K. The uniqueness-of-topology clause for the finite separable extension E/K identifies these topologies.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed p.374: dense embedding of henselian valued fields and the displayed Galois-group isomorphism.

proof.text: Density in L implies density of K in the subspace E: each open neighbourhood in E is the intersection of E with an open set of L, and that open set meets K. Intersect the Krasner neighbourhood of a in N with E and choose b in K in this neighbourhood. Krasner implies a in K(b)=K. If a was already in K the assertion was immediate, covering the empty moving-conjugate case. Convert the valuations using the actual value groups so their ball topologies agree.
